sentences.zh: 这是英国旨在解救数十名欧洲人质的远征行动的一部分。

sentences.en: There's pile-driving machinery.
sentences.zh: 有打桩机械。

sentences.en: And so by the new year of 1868, they have landed 13,000 soldiers, 20 miles of railway track, and 44 elephants,
sentences.zh: 因此，到了1868年新年之际，他们已经登陆了13,000名士兵、20英里长的铁轨和44头大象，

sentences.en: which were shipped across the Indian Ocean in specially reinforced transports.
sentences.zh: 这些大象是用经过特别加固的运输船横渡印度洋运过来的。

sentences.en: That is seven more elephants than Hannibal took.
sentences.zh: 这比汉尼拔带的大象还多出七头。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Seven more?
sentences.zh: 多七头？

sentences.en: To Italy, yeah.
sentences.zh: 去意大利的，对。

sentences.en: Hurrah from Napier.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔（Napier）万岁。

sentences.en: And while they're doing that, their sappers are literally blasting away through the cliffs to find the best route to get to the Highland Plateau.
sentences.zh: 正当他们在做这些事时，他们的工兵正用炸药炸开悬崖，寻找通往高原的最佳路线。

sentences.en: So they're going to have to head up 8,000 feet above sea level,
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须攀升到海拔8,000英尺的高度，

sentences.en: and then they're going to have to travel through the kind of gorges and the ravines for another 350 miles until they get to Magdala.
sentences.zh: 然后他们还得穿过各种峡谷和沟壑再走350英里，直到到达马格达拉（Magdala）。

sentences.en: On the 7th of January, Napier himself comes ashore from the SS Octavia.
sentences.zh: 1月7日，纳皮尔本人从“奥克塔维亚”号（SS Octavia）上岸。

sentences.en: And Napier, like all proficient commanders, has a great sense of theater, political theater.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔和所有出色的指挥官一样，极具戏剧天赋，懂得政治作秀。

sentences.en: He is dressed in his full uniform.
sentences.zh: 他身穿全套制服。

sentences.en: He's got all his medals.
sentences.zh: 佩戴着所有的勋章。

sentences.en: The ship's guns are firing a salute.
sentences.zh: 舰炮鸣礼炮。

sentences.en: There's a marine band playing.
sentences.zh: 海军军乐队在演奏。

sentences.en: He comes ashore.
sentences.zh: 他上岸了。

sentences.en: Everyone cheers.
sentences.zh: 所有人都欢呼雀跃。

sentences.en: And Napier is a – I mean, he's a very, very proficient commander.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔是一个——我的意思是，他是一个非常非常出色的指挥官。

sentences.en: He's not bothered about the costs.
sentences.zh: 他从不在乎成本。

sentences.en: He says, look, the government of India will pay, and the British government will back them up.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，印度政府会付钱的，英国政府会支持他们的。

sentences.en: I want more mule drivers.
sentences.zh: 我需要更多的骡夫。

sentences.en: My men need more boots.
sentences.zh: 我的人需要更多的靴子。

sentences.en: His men love him for this reason.
sentences.zh: 他的人民正是因为这一点而爱戴他。

sentences.en: And within a couple of weeks, they have started work on the railway, and the railway will bring all their supplies inland from the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 在几周之内，他们就开始修建铁路了，这条铁路将把所有物资从海岸运往内陆。

sentences.en: And they've also set up – I mean, this is an incredible achievement – they have basically a field telegraph all the way to their advance guard.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还建立了一个——我的意思是，这是一项不可思议的成就——他们基本上拉通了一条直达前哨部队的野战电报线。

sentences.en: They'll travel with that the whole way, basically unspooling copper wire as they go.
sentences.zh: 他们将一路带着它前行，基本上是一边走一边铺设铜线。

sentences.en: So by the 25th of January, 1868, Napier is ready to set off for the great trek to Magdala.
sentences.zh: 因此，到1868年1月25日，纳皮尔已经准备好启程前往马格达拉进行伟大远征了。

sentences.en: And as planned, he has 5,000 men that will go ahead as the spearhead.
sentences.zh: 按计划，他有5,000人作为先头部队先行。

sentences.en: And behind, he has 7,000 men who will guard his supply lines.
sentences.zh: 在后面，他有7,000人负责保卫补给线。

sentences.en: And as they set off, they must look absolutely outlandish to the locals.
sentences.zh: 当他们出发时，在当地人眼里，他们一定显得极其怪异。

sentences.en: I mean, it must look like people have landed from Mars or something, because the British cavalry lead the way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来一定像是火星人登陆或者别的什么，因为英国骑兵在前面带路。

sentences.en: And when I say British, this is British and Indian.
sentences.zh: 当我说英国时，这是英国和印度的联合部队。

sentences.en: There are Sikhs, there are recruits from across the Indian subcontinent.
sentences.zh: 有锡克教徒，也有来自印度次大陆各地的应征士兵。

sentences.en: So there's lots of, you know, people in turbans and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道，有很多缠着头巾之类的人。

sentences.en: But they're all wearing their British Army red jackets.
sentences.zh: 但他们都穿着英国陆军的红色夹克。

sentences.en: Then there's a supply chain seven miles long behind them.
sentences.zh: 随后是长达七英里的补给线。

sentences.en: There are the 44 elephants who are dragging the field guns, the kind of heavy guns.
sentences.zh: 有44头大象拖曳着野战炮，也就是那种重型火炮。

sentences.en: God, T.R.
sentences.zh: 天哪，T.R.

sentences.en: Dross would love that.
sentences.zh: 德罗斯（Dross）一定会喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, that's all his Christmases come at once.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直就像过年一样高兴。

sentences.en: And they have military bands playing the whole time.
sentences.zh: 而且他们全程都有军乐队在演奏。

sentences.en: So, I mean, they're basically like a sort of roaming orchestra.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他们基本上就像一个巡回乐团。

sentences.en: And they trudge into the highlands, making very slow progress.
sentences.zh: 他们跋涉进入高地，进展非常缓慢。

sentences.en: Napier is, of course, conscious.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔当然心知肚明。

sentences.en: The big issue that they face is if people attack them en route, if the warlords attack them.
sentences.zh: 他们面临的最大问题是如果在途中遭到袭击，如果军阀袭击他们的话。

sentences.en: And the key moment really comes at the end of February.
sentences.zh: 关键时刻确实出现在2月底。

sentences.en: So they've been on the road for a month or so.
sentences.zh: 所以他们已经在路上走了一个月左右。

sentences.en: And he enters the territory of one of Teodros' key rivals, who is a guy called Raskasa, who is the king of Tigray.
sentences.zh: 他进入了特奥多罗斯（Teodros）一个主要对手的领地，那是一个名叫拉斯卡萨（Raskasa）的人，他是提格雷（Tigray）的国王。

sentences.en: And basically, the road to Magdalene runs through this kingdom of Tigray.
sentences.zh: 基本上，通往马格达拉的路要穿过这个提格雷王国。

sentences.en: And Napier, he's a great diplomat.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔是个伟大的外交家。

sentences.en: He waits for this guy.
sentences.zh: 他在等这个人。

sentences.en: He stops.
sentences.zh: 他停了下来。

sentences.en: He waits.
sentences.zh: 他在等待。

sentences.en: He wants to greet him with full military honors.
sentences.zh: 他想以全套军礼迎接他。

sentences.en: He has his troops drawn up very smartly.
sentences.zh: 他的部队列队严整。

sentences.en: When this bloke arrives, he says, would you like to inspect our guns?
sentences.zh: 当这家伙到达时，他说，你想检阅我们的军队吗？

sentences.en: I've brought you presents.
sentences.zh: 我给你带了礼物。

sentences.en: I've brought you an Arabian horse.
sentences.zh: 我给你带来了一匹阿拉伯马。

sentences.en: I've got your rifle for you.
sentences.zh: 我为你准备了步枪。

sentences.en: I've got some nice glassware for you.
sentences.zh: 我为你准备了一些漂亮的玻璃器皿。

sentences.en: And he says to Kassa, my troops will not loot.
sentences.zh: 他对卡萨（Kassa）说，我的部队绝不劫掠。

sentences.en: They will not steal so much as a kind of, you know, a loaf of bread.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不会偷一块面包之类的小东西。

sentences.en: We will pay for every sack of grain.
sentences.zh: 每一袋谷物我们都会付钱。

sentences.en: If you help us, I promise you the friendship of Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 如果你帮助我们，我向你保证维多利亚女王的友谊。

sentences.en: And it works very well.
sentences.zh: 这非常有效。

sentences.en: This guy says to him, well, you're a very impressive person.
sentences.zh: 这家伙对他说，嗯，你是一个令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: He gives him a lion's skin cloak and he says, I will bring you weekly supplies of food, which he does.
sentences.zh: 他送给纳皮尔一件狮皮斗篷，并说我会每周给你运送食物，他也确实做到了。

sentences.en: And I think there's an implicit understanding here.
sentences.zh: 我想这里有一种心照不宣的默契。

sentences.en: It is never written down and it's never explicitly stated.
sentences.zh: 这从未被写成文字，也从未被明确表述过。

sentences.en: But I think it's pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这相当清楚。

sentences.en: And Napier knows this man expects him to deal with Teodros once and for all.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔也知道这个人指望他一劳永逸地解决特奥多罗斯。

sentences.en: That that is the quid pro quo.
sentences.zh: 这就是等价交换。

sentences.en: So you've been comparing this to the conquistadors in America.
sentences.zh: 所以你一直在把这与美洲的 conquistadors（征服者）进行比较。

sentences.en: And this is a very familiar story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常熟悉的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, whether it's the Aztecs or the Incas, that the local, not necessarily even subject peoples,
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论是阿兹特克人还是印加人，当地人——甚至不一定是臣民，

sentences.en: but inferior rivals who want to throw off the hegemony of the local big power that they team up with the Europeans.
sentences.zh: 而是那些想要摆脱当地大国霸权的地位较低的竞争对手——他们与欧洲人结盟。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly it.
sentences.zh: 我想事实确实如此。

sentences.en: But the difference, I guess, is that the British don't want to stay.
sentences.zh: 但我想区别在于，英国人并不想留下来。

sentences.en: You know, the conquistadors want to stay.
sentences.zh: 你知道，征服者是想留下来的。

sentences.en: They have their own agenda.
sentences.zh: 他们有他们自己的议程。

sentences.en: The British really just didn't want to get in and get out.
sentences.zh: 英国人其实只是想进去然后出来。

sentences.en: Now, this is probably a good point to ask.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能是个好时机来问问。

sentences.en: What has happened to the hostages?
sentences.zh: 人质们怎么了？

sentences.en: We haven't seen them for a while.
sentences.zh: 我们有一段时间没见到他们了。

sentences.en: So we last saw them in the summer of 1867, so almost a year ago.
sentences.zh: 我们上次见到他们是在1867年夏天，也就是差不多一年前。

sentences.en: What have they been up to?
sentences.zh: 他们一直在做什么？

sentences.en: They've been stuck in their huts at Magdala.
sentences.zh: 他们一直被困在马格达拉的棚屋里。

sentences.en: They've been playing cards.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在打牌。

sentences.en: And I mean, they're kind of manacled.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们身上都戴着镣铐。

sentences.en: So I don't know how easy that is.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道那有多容易。

sentences.en: But I suppose they're bent over.
sentences.zh: 不过我想他们是弯着腰的。

sentences.en: I mean, cards is one thing you can do if you're bent over.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，弯着腰能做的一件事就是打牌。

sentences.en: They've been reading the Bible.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在读圣经。

sentences.en: They're allowed to use all their old stores.
sentences.zh: 他们被允许使用他们所有的旧存货。

sentences.en: And actually, so they've been eating very well at Magdala because they brought up a lot of their old kind of stores and stuff.
sentences.zh: 实际上，所以在马格达拉他们吃得很好，因为他们带了许多过去的存货之类的东西。

sentences.en: So insanely, they've been having like four course meals, soup, a starter, a main course and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以疯狂的是，他们一直在吃四道菜的饭，有汤、前菜、主菜等等。

sentences.en: So that's the good news.
sentences.zh: 所以这是好消息。

sentences.en: The bad news is they're still in chains.
sentences.zh: 坏消息是他们仍然戴着铁链。

sentences.en: Some of them are very ill.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人病得很重。

sentences.en: They're very depressed.
sentences.zh: 他们非常沮丧。

sentences.en: But then in December 1867, a traveler arrived in Magdala with a message for Dr. Blanc.
sentences.zh: 但随后在1867年12月，一名旅行者抵达马格达拉，给布朗医生（Dr. Blanc）带来了一个口信。

sentences.en: And this was the news that the British had landed on the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 这个消息就是英国人已经在海岸登陆了。

sentences.en: The first British sort of engineers had landed on the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 第一批英国工程师已经登陆了海岸。

sentences.en: Dr. Blanc said later,
sentences.zh: 布朗医生后来回忆说，

sentences.en: it was one of those exciting moments in a man's life that few can realize who have not passed through months of mental agony and then been suddenly overcome with joy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人一生中极少数激动人心的时刻之一，只有那些经历过数月精神折磨随后又突然被喜悦淹没的人才能体会。

sentences.en: So it's tremendously exciting for the hostages.
sentences.zh: 所以这对人质来说是极其令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: The British are on their way.
sentences.zh: 英国人在路上了。

sentences.en: But of course, they're now in a state of unbearable tension because Teodros has been gone for years, two years almoSt.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他们现在处于一种无法忍受的紧张状态，因为特奥多罗斯已经离开好几年了，快两年了。

sentences.en: Will Teodros get back to Magdala before the British?
sentences.zh: 特奥多罗斯会在英国人之前赶回马格达拉吗？

sentences.en: And if so, will he have them all killed or will he agree to see sense?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，他会把他们全部杀死，还是会恢复理智？

sentences.en: They don't know.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道。

sentences.en: And this, of course, brings us to Teodros himself.
sentences.zh: 当然，这把我们带回了特奥多罗斯本人。

sentences.en: As I said, he's been gone for ages on campaign.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他外出征战已经很久了。

sentences.en: He has been fighting rebels and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他一直在与叛军等人作战。

sentences.en: But that autumn, 1867, he too began to head inland.
sentences.zh: 但在1867年那个秋天，他也开始向内陆进发。

sentences.en: He left his northern capital to head back to Magdala.
sentences.zh: 他离开北方首都，启程返回马格达拉。

sentences.en: And with him, he brought his army.
sentences.zh: 随他一起的还有他的军队。

sentences.en: He brought a huge horde of camp followers, a huge horde of prisoners that he had taken.
sentences.zh: 他带了一大群随军家属，以及他俘获的一大群囚犯。

sentences.en: So he's got about 50,000 people with him and above all, his favorite things, which are his guns.
sentences.zh: 所以他身边大约有50,000人，最重要的是他最喜欢的东西——他的大炮。

sentences.en: So listeners may remember that he was getting these Swiss and German missionaries to try and build guns for him.
sentences.zh: 听众们可能还记得，他曾让这些瑞士和德国传教士试图为他制造大炮。

sentences.en: And they have finally managed to cast what he really wanted, which is a giant mortar.
sentences.zh: 他们终于设法铸造了他真正想要的东西，那就是一门巨型迫击炮。

sentences.en: And this is a 70 ton mortar.
sentences.zh: 这是一门70吨重的迫击炮。

sentences.en: Its mouth is two feet wide.
sentences.zh: 它的炮口有两英尺宽。

sentences.en: So it's a huge caliber.
sentences.zh: 所以它的口径非常巨大。

sentences.en: And he calls it Sebastopol because he loves the Crimean War.
sentences.zh: 他把它叫做塞瓦斯托波尔（Sebastopol），因为他太热爱克里米亚战争了。

sentences.en: So Napier had been told Teodros has got these guns.
sentences.zh: 所以纳皮尔听说特奥多罗斯有这些大炮。

sentences.en: And Napier assumed, well, when Teodros goes back to Magdala, he'll obviously leave these guns behind because they're so heavy.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔以为，当特奥多罗斯返回马格达拉时，他显然会把这些大炮留下，因为它们太重了。

sentences.en: And he's not going to try and drag them.
sentences.zh: 而且他不会去尝试拖拽它们。

sentences.en: But no, Teodros is dragging these guns back to Magdala.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，特奥多罗斯正把这些大炮拖回马格达拉。

sentences.en: And he's very excited about the chance of using them.
sentences.zh: 他对使用它们的机会感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Can I ask, Dominic, these missionaries, these Swiss and German missionaries, obviously making guns, we said in the first episode, isn't really part of what they're about.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克（Dominic），请问这些传教士，这些瑞士和德国传教士，显然在制造枪炮，我们在第一集里说过，这其实并不是他们的本职工作。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But have they upped their game by this point?
sentences.zh: 但到这个时候，他们是不是已经加大了干劲？

sentences.en: Are these functioning?
sentences.zh: 这些武器能运作吗？

sentences.en: Well, that is a great question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真是个好问题。

sentences.en: And do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: We're going to find out.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会知道了。

sentences.en: We're going to find out what happens.
sentences.zh: 我们会知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Because Teodros...
sentences.zh: 因为特奥多罗斯……

sentences.en: Teodros has not yet fired it.
sentences.zh: 特奥多罗斯还没开过炮呢。

sentences.en: Teodros has experimented a little bit with these guns, but he's never really fired them in anger.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯对这些枪支做过一些小实验，但他从来没有真正实战开过火。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Exciting.
sentences.zh: 太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: And this is something for listeners to look forward to.
sentences.zh: 这也是听众们可以期待的看点。

sentences.en: Now, he knows at this point, so let's say we're at the beginning of 1868, he knows the British have landed.
sentences.zh: 现在，他此时已经知道了，假设我们处在1868年年初，他知道英国人已经登陆了。

sentences.en: His agents have intercepted messages from Napier to the local chiefs, you know, basically trying to get the local chiefs' support.
sentences.zh: 他的特工拦截了纳皮尔发给当地酋长的信件，你知道的，基本上是试图争取当地酋长的支持。

sentences.en: Teodros' reaction, people who are fans of his erratic behavior will be pleased to hear that he reacts in a very peculiar way.
sentences.zh: 至于特沃德罗斯的反应嘛，喜欢他那种反复无常行为的粉丝们会很高兴听到他的反应非常奇特。

sentences.en: So, first of all, he says to his German missionary gunsmiths, he says, this is brilliant news.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，他对他的德国传教士枪匠说，这真是个绝妙的消息。

sentences.en: The one thing I've always wanted to see is a really disciplined European army, and finally I'm going to get the chance.
sentences.zh: 我一直最想看的就是一支纪律严明的欧洲军队，而我终于有机会见到了。

sentences.en: So, his plan appears to be that he will get to Magdala first, he will line up all his guns, then he will test them against the British army.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的计划似乎是先赶到马格达拉，排好他所有的枪，然后用它们来和英国军队较量一番。

sentences.en: He thinks that when the British see Sebastopol in action, they will respect him, and they will see what a great king he is.
sentences.zh: 他认为，当英国人看到“塞瓦斯托波尔”大炮开火时，他们就会敬畏他，并看到他是一位多么伟大的国王。

sentences.en: And what an impressive person he is, and they'll definitely want to come to an arrangement with him and perhaps sign a treaty.
sentences.zh: 以及他是多么令人印象深刻的一个人，他们肯定会想和他达成协议，也许还会签个条约。

sentences.en: This is his thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的想法。

sentences.en: He tells his courtiers, he says, I've heard a prophecy that a European king will meet with an Ethiopian king in this country, and after this, a great king will come.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他的朝臣们，我听说过一个预言，说一个欧洲国王将在这片土地上与一个埃塞俄比亚国王会面，在这之后，一位伟大的国王将会出现。

sentences.en: But I don't know whether I shall be that great king or someone else.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道我是否会成为那个伟大的国王，还是另有其人。

sentences.en: That's modest of him.
sentences.zh: 他还挺谦虚的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Even so, you know, he's very keen.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，你知道的，他非常热切。

sentences.en: He's very excited.
sentences.zh: 他非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He's also started rebombarding his old crush, Hormuzd Rassam, the British agent, the guy from Mosul who used to be an archaeologist in the British descent.
sentences.zh: 他还开始重新狂热追求他的老心上人霍尔木兹·拉萨姆，也就是那个英国特工，那个来自摩苏尔、曾是英国后裔考古学家的人。

sentences.en: But is he still chained up at this point?
sentences.zh: 但此时他还被锁着吗？

sentences.en: He's chained up at Magdala in the mountain lair, but Teodras has started writing, sending him love letters again.
sentences.zh: 他被锁在山中巢穴马格达拉，但特沃德罗斯又开始给他写信、送情书了。

sentences.en: I mean, an insane thing to write to somebody who you were keeping as a hostage.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对一个被你当做人质囚禁的人写这种信，简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: How are you, my friend?
sentences.zh: 你好吗，我的朋友？

sentences.en: The nearer I approach towards you, the happier I feel.
sentences.zh: 我越是靠近你，我就感到越快乐。

sentences.en: Oh, my friend, do not think I bear any hatred towards you.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的朋友，不要以为我对你怀有任何恨意。

sentences.en: I've placed you in a present position in order that I may come to know the people of your country.
sentences.zh: 我把你安置在目前的位置，是为了让我能够了解你们国家的人民。

sentences.en: It's kind of the opposite of the Stockholm syndrome, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这有点像斯德哥尔摩综合征的反面，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的，在这里是你的绑架者。

sentences.zh: 绑架者爱上了被绑架者。

sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And the mad thing, the maddest thing is that Teodras says to him, the thing I'm really looking forward to is I can't wait to show you, Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 而最疯狂的事情，最疯狂的事情是特沃德罗斯对他说，我真正期待的是，我等不及要向你展示“塞瓦斯托波尔”了。

sentences.en: I have had a large mortar cast, which is to tame me on the road.
sentences.zh: 我铸造了一门大迫击炮，它将一路上驯服我。

sentences.en: But when I reach Magdala and you see it and admire it, I will forget all the trouble it has given me.
sentences.zh: 但当我到达马格达拉，你看到并赞赏它时，我就会忘记它给我带来的所有麻烦。

sentences.en: So basically, Sebastopol for Teodras is a bit like the owl man for the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，“塞瓦斯托波尔”对特沃德罗斯来说有点像阿兹特克人眼中的猫头鹰人。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: It's the ultimate weapon that will definitely win him the war.
sentences.zh: 这是绝对能帮他赢得战争的终极武器。

sentences.zh: 它将为他赢得战争，也将为他赢得拉萨姆永恒的喜爱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So finally, Teodras arrives at the mountaintop on the 27th of March, 1868.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，特沃德罗斯于1868年3月27日抵达山顶。

sentences.en: It's a very Gothic scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常哥特式的场景。

sentences.en: So a storm is breaking overhead, thunder, pouring rain.
sentences.zh: 头顶上电闪雷鸣，大雨倾盆。

sentences.en: He arrives on the mountaintop and his guards immediately bring in Rossam.
sentences.zh: 他一到山顶，卫兵就把拉萨姆带了进来。

sentences.en: And Rossam is shocked to see that Teodras has aged a lot in the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 拉萨姆震惊地发现，特沃德罗斯在过去几年里老了很多。

sentences.en: He looks very gaunt, very haggard.
sentences.zh: 他看起来非常消瘦、憔悴。

sentences.zh: 现在，拉萨姆的状态可能没保持得有多好，因为他一直被锁在小屋里，但特沃德罗斯一直在外征战。

sentences.en: His mental health isn't great, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他的心理健康状况不太好。

sentences.zh: 他迎向拉萨姆——他的人质，在英国人入侵他国家的背景下，说出了这样一句疯狂的问候：今天我们必须全都是英国人。

sentences.en: And what does he mean by that?
sentences.zh: 他这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: God knows.
sentences.zh: 鬼知道。

sentences.zh: 穿不适合炎热气温的衣服。

sentences.zh: 用那种漫不经心的轻描淡写来应对一切。

sentences.zh: 不，他喜欢情绪激昂的爆发。

sentences.en: No, I think what he means by this, he means he's just, I think he just is so excited that the British are coming in a weird way.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得他这话的意思是，我觉得他只是，用一种诡异的方式，因为英国人要来而感到太兴奋了。

sentences.en: And he says, I can't wait to show you Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 他说，我等不及要向你展示“塞瓦斯托波尔”了。

sentences.en: And he says, the two happiest days in my life are when Sebastopol was cast, and also today, when I get to see you again.
sentences.zh: 他说，我一生中最快乐的两天，一是铸造“塞瓦斯托波尔”的时候，还有就是今天，我又见到你了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so unsettling.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太让人不安了。

sentences.zh: 我们的制作人卡勒姆会喜欢这个梗的。

sentences.zh: 在《我是阿兰·帕特里奇》里有个场景，阿兰·帕特里奇实际上被一个叫杰德的狂热粉丝当成了俘虏。

sentences.en: And this is basically Rossam's situation.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是拉萨姆的处境。

sentences.zh: 他被特沃德罗斯俘虏了。

sentences.en: But then Teodros' mood changes abruptly, and he says to Rossam, I hope, Mr. Rossam, that when your people arrive, they will not despise me because I am black.
sentences.zh: 但随后特沃德罗斯的情绪骤然转变，他对拉萨姆说，拉萨姆先生，我希望当你们的人到达时，他们不会因为我是黑人而鄙视我。

sentences.en: And then, a note of fatalism.
sentences.zh: 然后，透出一丝宿命论。

sentences.en: One day you may see me dead, and while you stand by my corpse, it may be that you curse me for my bad conduct towards you.
sentences.zh: 有一天你可能会看到我死去，而当你站在我的尸体旁时，也许你会因为我对你的不良行径而诅咒我。

sentences.en: Rossam, I think, finds it hard to know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得拉萨姆很难去理解。

sentences.en: Keep up with all this.
sentences.zh: 完全跟不上这一切。

sentences.en: Yeah, keep up.
sentences.zh: 对，跟不上。

sentences.en: And the maddest thing of all, right?
sentences.zh: 而最疯狂的是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: So, Teodros, almost tearful with his love of Rossam and, you know, morbid thoughts and all this.
sentences.zh: 所以，特沃德罗斯对拉萨姆的爱几乎要喜极而泣，还有那些病态的想法等等。

sentences.en: And then, as soon as his guards take Rossam out, Teodros turns to his courteous and says very bitterly,
sentences.zh: 然后，卫兵刚把拉萨姆带出去，特沃德罗斯就转向他的朝臣，非常怨恨地说道，

sentences.en: Rossam has made asses of us and a fool of me.
sentences.zh: 拉萨姆把我们当傻子耍，把我当成个笨蛋。

sentences.en: He's pretending to be my friend, but he's been plotting to slaughter us, ravish our wives, and reduce our people to bondage.
sentences.zh: 他假装是我的朋友，但实际上他一直在密谋屠杀我们、蹂躏我们的妻子，并把我们的人民沦为奴役。

sentences.zh: 这有点像怀春的16岁少女。

sentences.zh: 完全就是这样。

sentences.zh: 这正是他对拉萨姆的态度。

sentences.en: Now, that's Teodros.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是特沃德罗斯。

sentences.en: General Napier, a very different kind of man with his…
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔将军，一个截然不同的人，留着……

sentences.en: His moustache and his keen interest in engineering project.
sentences.zh: 留着小胡子，对工程项目充满热情。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: His men have now trudged all the way to the edge of the Jidder Gorge, which is about 50 miles from Magdala.
sentences.zh: 他的人马现在已经长途跋涉来到了吉德峡谷边缘，这里距离马格达拉大约50英里。

sentences.en: We're now early April.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是四月初了。

sentences.en: So, this is very sort of sun-scorched, barren terrain.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一片阳光炙烤的贫瘠土地。

sentences.en: It's hard work now.
sentences.zh: 现在走得很辛苦。

sentences.en: They're a long way from the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们距离海岸已经很远了。

sentences.en: They've traveled more than 300 miles.
sentences.zh: 他们已经走了300多英里。

sentences.en: And on the 6th of April, they get their first glance of the summit of Magdala in the distance.
sentences.zh: 4月6日，他们在远处第一次瞥见了马格达拉的山顶。

sentences.en: So, one war correspondent said it rose like a great ship out of the surrounding billows.
sentences.zh: 因此，一位战地记者说，它就像一艘巨轮从周围的波涛中升起。

sentences.en: And Napier now sends ahead a messenger with a final ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔现在派出一名信使，带去最后通牒。

sentences.en: By command of the Queen of England, I am approaching Magdala with my army in order to recover from your hands,
sentences.zh: 奉英国女王陛下之命，我正率领军队接近马格达拉，以便从你们手中收回，

sentences.en: Envoy Rossam, Consul Cameron, Dr. Blanc, Lieutenant Prido, and the other Europeans now in your majesty's power.
sentences.zh: 特使拉萨姆、卡梅伦领事、布兰克医生、普里多中尉以及目前在你陛下权力之下的其他欧洲人。

sentences.en: I request your majesty to send them to my camp as soon as it is sufficiently near to admit of their coming in safety.
sentences.zh: 我要求陛下在营地足够近、允许他们安全进入时，将他们送到我的营地。

sentences.en: There is no reply.
sentences.zh: 没有回复。

sentences.en: But Teodros does know that the British are very close now.
sentences.zh: 但特沃德罗斯确实知道英国人现在已经非常近了。

sentences.en: Now, every morning, Teodros very excitedly has been scanning the mountains with his telescope.
sentences.zh: 现在，每天早上，特沃德罗斯都极其兴奋地用望远镜搜寻着群山。

sentences.en: Is that the telescope he got given?
sentences.zh: 那是别人送给他的那支望远镜吗？

sentences.zh: 他把它扔了。

sentences.zh: 所以，他没有把它砸碎。

sentences.en: No, clearly it didn't break.

sentences.zh: 他一直透过望远镜凝视着。

sentences.en: And on the 7th of April, which is the Tuesday before Easter, he sees the first red British uniforms on the other side of the Bishilo Gorge.
sentences.zh: 在4月7日，也就是复活节前的星期二，他在比希洛峡谷的另一侧看到了第一批穿红色英国军服的人。

sentences.en: And he shouts, perhaps unexpectedly, he shouts very loudly with excitement when he sees them.
sentences.zh: 他大喊大叫，也许出乎意料的是，当他看到他们时，他兴奋地大声喊叫。

sentences.en: He shouts, hurrah, there go the donkeys.
sentences.zh: 他喊道，万岁，驴子们来了。

sentences.en: Does he, the donkeys are the British?
sentences.zh: 是吗，驴子是指英国人？

sentences.en: Not all these mules that Napier's had brought over.
sentences.zh: 不，是纳皮尔带过来的那些骡子。

sentences.en: The British have got mules with them, so maybe that's what he's talking about.
sentences.zh: 英国人带了骡子随行，所以也许他指的是这个。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: And then he hands the telescope to this Swiss missionary called Theophilus Valmire, who he's very keen on.
sentences.zh: 然后他把望远镜递给了一个叫狄奥菲勒斯·瓦尔迈尔的瑞士传教士，他很喜欢这个人。

sentences.en: And he says to Valmire in a very jaunty way,

sentences.en: So, the next day is a Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 所以，第二天是星期三。

sentences.en: Theodros gets up before dawn.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯在黎明前起床。

sentences.en: Now, usually he dressed quite austerely with a white robe and a red border.
sentences.zh: 平时他的穿着相当朴素，是一件白袍配红边。

sentences.en: But today, because the British have come, he's very excited.
sentences.zh: 但今天，因为英国人来了，他非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He's wearing, we're told, a silk gold-threaded robe with white pantaloons.
sentences.zh: 据说他穿着一件金线织成的丝绸长袍，搭配白色宽松长裤。

sentences.en: And Rassam said, rather disparagingly, he looked more like a harlequin than a sovereign.
sentences.zh: 拉萨姆贬损地评价说，他看起来与其说像个君主，倒不如说像个丑角。

sentences.en: And it's something really sad about that.
sentences.zh: 这其中真有一种让人难过的情绪。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: He's trying to look regal.
sentences.zh: 他试图展现出王者的风范。

sentences.en: He's trying to make a splash, only to be the victim of massive British snobbery.
sentences.zh: 他试图引起轰动，结果却成了英国人严重势利心态的受害者。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 他穿错了衣服。

sentences.zh: 你知道特沃德罗斯会和谁绝对相处得超级融洽吗？

sentences.zh: 就在这时，特沃德罗斯下令把所有囚犯都带下来。

sentences.en: And so they let these people go.

sentences.zh: 然后特沃德罗斯集结了军队，对将士们发表了一场极其疯狂的演讲。

sentences.en: He starts to inspire them.
sentences.zh: 他开始鼓舞他们的士气。

sentences.en: He says, the British are coming and be in no doubt, the British are much better than we are.
sentences.zh: 他说，英国人要来了，毫无疑问，英国人比我们强得多。

sentences.zh: 他们装备更好，实力更强。

sentences.zh: 看着她们。

sentences.en: They bring you clothes and riches and pay.
sentences.zh: 她们给你带去了衣服、财富和赏赐。

sentences.en: Go down and help yourselves.
sentences.zh: 冲下去，自取所需吧。

sentences.en: And at this moment, you know, proper Hollywood stuff.
sentences.zh: 而就在这时，你知道的，典型的荷里活桥段。

sentences.en: The storm breaks.
sentences.zh: 风暴骤起。

sentences.en: There's a great crash of thunder overhead.
sentences.zh: 头顶上雷声轰鸣。

sentences.en: And at that moment, Teodros shouts to his gunners, open fire.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，特沃德罗斯朝他的炮手大喊，开火。

sentences.en: And the first shells shriek through the air towards Napier's men.
sentences.zh: 第一批炮弹尖啸着划破空气，飞向内皮尔的手下。

sentences.en: So some of the guns are working.
sentences.zh: 看来这些大炮还能用。

sentences.en: And at that point down below, the Abyssinian troops that have been waiting gave a great kind of cheer and a kind of war whoop.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，下方一直在等待的阿比西尼亚军队发出了一声巨大的欢呼和一种类似战斗呐喊的声音。

sentences.en: And they charge onto the plane themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己冲上了平原。

sentences.en: Some of them on horseback.
sentences.zh: 有些人骑着马。

sentences.en: Some of them running.
sentences.zh: 有些人跑着。

sentences.en: They've leveled their spears.
sentences.zh: 他们平举着长矛。

sentences.en: They're singing their war songs.
sentences.zh: 他们高唱着战歌。

sentences.en: It's the kind of ride of the Rahirim.
sentences.zh: 这就像是洛汗骑兵的冲锋。

sentences.en: At the Battle of the Pelennor Fields or something.
sentences.zh: 就像帕兰诺平原战役之类的场景。

sentences.en: And a tremendously rousing and exciting moment as they race towards the British.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其振奋人心的时刻，他们向英军狂奔而去。

sentences.en: And for a moment, you know, if you're watching the film of this, it looks as if Teodros' plan has worked.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，如果你在看相关的电影，你会觉得特沃德罗斯的计划成功了。

sentences.en: It looks as if the British have walked right into a trap.
sentences.zh: 看起来英军好像直接走进了陷阱。

sentences.en: They've walked into the guns.
sentences.zh: 他们走进了炮火的射程。

sentences.en: They've walked into the charge.
sentences.zh: 他们走进了冲锋圈。

sentences.en: And they're going to be swept off the plateau.
sentences.zh: 他们将被横扫出这片高原。

sentences.en: But it doesn't quite work out that way.
sentences.zh: 但事情的发展并非如此。

sentences.en: So first of all, the guns.
sentences.zh: 首先是这些大炮。

sentences.en: These guns that he loved so much.
sentences.zh: 这些他如此钟爱的大炮。

sentences.en: I mean, never get a missionary to build you a gun.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，千万别找传教士来为你造炮。

sentences.en: That's the lesson of history.
sentences.zh: 这就是历史给我们的教训。

sentences.en: It is the lesson of history.
sentences.zh: 这确实是历史的教训。

sentences.en: A Swiss missionary.
sentences.zh: 一个瑞士传教士。

sentences.en: The guns are so inaccurate that the shells just sail over the heads of Napier and his men.
sentences.zh: 这些大炮精准度太差，炮弹直接从内皮尔及其手下的头顶飞了过去。

sentences.en: Has he fired Sebastopol at this point?
sentences.zh: 此时他发射“塞瓦斯托波尔”大炮了吗？

sentences.en: I don't know that he ever does fire Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他到底有没有发射过“塞瓦斯托波尔”。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，没有。

sentences.en: But one of the guns early on, one of the guns explodes.
sentences.zh: 但其中一门大炮在刚开始时就爆炸了。

sentences.en: It bursts.
sentences.zh: 它炸裂了。

sentences.en: And at this point, I think some of the gunners lost heart.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，我想有些炮手开始丧失斗志了。

sentences.en: Shoddy Swiss workmanship.
sentences.zh: 粗制滥造的瑞士工艺。

sentences.en: So off in the way with the Swiss, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以瑞士制造也就这水平，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，不是吗？

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, his assault troops or whatever are charging at the British.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他的突击部队之类的正在向英军冲锋。

sentences.en: Now, the British are taking aim at their rifles.
sentences.zh: 此时，英军正举枪瞄准。

sentences.en: But the Abyssinians know.
sentences.zh: 但阿比西尼亚人心里清楚。

sentences.en: Yeah, they've charged guns before.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们以前就冲击过大炮阵地。

sentences.en: They've charged riflemen before.
sentences.zh: 他们以前就冲击过步兵防线。

sentences.en: They know that basically what will happen is the riflemen will fire, but then they'll have to reload.
sentences.zh: 他们知道基本上会发生的情况是，步兵会开枪，但接着他们必须重新装填弹药。

sentences.en: That's a massive faff.
sentences.zh: 那可真是个巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: It takes them ages.
sentences.zh: 那要花他们好一阵子。

sentences.en: And you can be on them and you can butcher them.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以冲上去把他们屠杀殆尽。

sentences.en: But what they don't know is the British have a secret technological advantage.
sentences.zh: 但他们不知道的是，英军拥有一项秘密的技术优势。

sentences.en: The British have bought, for the first time, state-of-the-art Snyder breech-loading rifles.
sentences.zh: 英军首次装备了最先进的斯奈德后装式步枪。

sentences.en: So these are rifles that you can reload with a breech in seconds.
sentences.zh: 所以这些步枪可以通过枪管后部在几秒钟内重新装弹。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We have got the Snyder breech-loading rifle and they have not.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有斯奈德后装步枪，而他们没有。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that means that collectively, the British line can fire about 30 to 40 rounds a second.
sentences.zh: 这意味着总体而言，英国防线的射速可以达到每秒30到40发。

sentences.en: And there's no let-up in the rate of fire.
sentences.zh: 而且火力持续不断，毫无喘息之机。

sentences.en: And so the Abyssinians are charging towards them, thinking at some point they're going to stop and they're going to reload.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿比西尼亚人正向他们冲锋，以为对方在某个时刻会停下来重新装弹。

sentences.en: And that moment never comes.
sentences.zh: 但那个时刻永远没有到来。

sentences.en: The first to fall are the Abyssinian chiefs and kind of captains because they are wearing bright red kind of scarlet shirts.
sentences.zh: 最先倒下的是阿比西尼亚的酋长和首领们，因为他们穿着鲜红色的衬衫。

sentences.en: That is ironic.
sentences.zh: 这真是具有讽刺意味。

sentences.en: So they're sitting ducks.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就像活靶子一样。

sentences.en: They are shot down.
sentences.zh: 他们被击落了。

sentences.en: Their men keep coming.
sentences.zh: 他们的人继续前进。

sentences.en: And then the bullets, just a hail of bullets, just knock them down in the hundreds.
sentences.zh: 然后子弹，密集的子弹，成百上千地将他们击倒。

sentences.en: And they keep charging.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍在冲锋。

sentences.en: They keep charging again and again.
sentences.zh: 他们一次又一次地继续冲锋。

sentences.en: The British just keep on firing.
sentences.zh: 英军只是不断地开火。

sentences.en: It is a total bloodbath.
sentences.zh: 这是一场彻底的血洗。

sentences.en: And from the heights, Theodros is watching and he just cannot believe it.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯在高处注视着这一切，简直难以置信。

sentences.en: So this continues for the next couple of hours.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了接下来的几个小时。

sentences.en: At last, dusk begins to fall and the fighting dies down.
sentences.zh: 终于，暮色开始降临，战斗渐渐平息。

sentences.en: And the survivors straggle back to Theodros' camp.
sentences.zh: 幸存者们零零落落地逃回了特沃德罗斯的营地。

sentences.en: And in the dark, he calls out to them, where is so-and-so?
sentences.zh: 在黑暗中，他大声呼喊着他们的名字，某某人在哪儿？

sentences.en: Where is so-and-so?
sentences.zh: 某某人在哪儿？

sentences.en: Naming his chiefs.
sentences.zh: 他点着他那些酋长的名字。

sentences.en: They're all dead.
sentences.zh: 他们都死了。

sentences.en: All the people he knows by name are dead.
sentences.zh: 所有他叫得出名字的人都死了。

sentences.en: So in all, he's lost about 1,000 men, just under 1,000 men, thousands more wounded.
sentences.zh: 总计，他失去了大约一千人，不到一千人，还有数千人受伤。

sentences.en: The British have lost two men killed and about 20 wounded.
sentences.zh: 英军阵亡两人，受伤约二十人。

sentences.en: I mean, you could hardly imagine a more lopsided battle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你很难想象还有比这更一边倒的战斗了。

sentences.en: Theodros is stunned.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯惊呆了。

sentences.en: I mean, the weird thing is he always kind of knew, I think, that the British would be a tough challenge.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，奇怪的是，我想他其实一直都知道英军会是一个强劲的对手。

sentences.en: But he didn't think they'd be this tough.
sentences.zh: 但他没想到他们会这么强硬。

sentences.en: And he retires to his tent in the sort of terrible silence.
sentences.zh: 他在一片可怕的寂静中退回了自己的帐篷。

sentences.en: He doesn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: Does he free the hostages?
sentences.zh: 他要释放人质吗？

sentences.en: Does he start killing the hostages?
sentences.zh: 他要开始杀害人质吗？

sentences.en: Does he try to run away?
sentences.zh: 他要尝试逃跑吗？

sentences.en: Well, when in doubt, send another of your letters to Rassam, I think is his general approach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当感到犹豫不决时，就再给拉萨姆写一封信，我想这就是他的一贯作风。

sentences.en: So he sends Rassam another of his mad notes.
sentences.zh: 于是他又给拉萨姆发送了一张他那疯疯癫癫的便条。

sentences.en: How have you passed the day?
sentences.zh: 你们这一天是怎么度过的？

sentences.en: Thank God I am well.
sentences.zh: 感谢上帝，我很好。

sentences.en: I, being a king, could not allow people to come and fight me without attacking them firSt.
sentences.zh: 我身为一国之君，绝不能容许别人前来攻打我而不首先发起反击。

sentences.en: I have done so, and my troops have been beaten.
sentences.zh: 我这么做了，而我的军队战败了。

sentences.en: I thought your people were women, but I find they are men.
sentences.zh: 我本以为你们的人都是女人，但我发现他们是真正的男子汉。

sentences.en: They fought very bravely.
sentences.zh: 他们战斗得非常勇敢。

sentences.en: Seeing that I'm unable to withstand them, I must ask you to reconcile me to them.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我无力抵挡他们，我必须请你协助我与他们言和。

sentences.en: And Rassam scribbles him a note and says, I completely agree.
sentences.zh: 拉萨姆草草写了一张便条回复他说，我完全同意。

sentences.en: At dawn, I think you should send a delegation to Napier.
sentences.zh: 拂晓时分，我想你应该派一个代表团去见内皮尔。

sentences.en: Maybe send that missionary, the Reverend Flad and Lieutenant Predo, and they can carry your peace offer to Napier.
sentences.zh: 也许可以派那个传教士弗拉德牧师和普雷多中尉，他们可以把你的求和提议带给内皮尔。

sentences.en: So that night, nobody can sleep because there's just a lot of wailing as the Abyssinians mourn their dead.
sentences.zh: 于是那天晚上，谁也无法入睡，因为阿比西尼亚人为死者哀悼的哭号声此起彼伏。

sentences.en: And at four o'clock in the morning, Teodros summons Flad and Predo, as Rassam suggested, and says, I want you to go down to the British camp and discuss peace.
sentences.zh: 清晨四点，特沃德罗斯按照拉萨姆的建议召来弗拉德和普雷多，说道，我要你们去英军营地商讨和平事宜。

sentences.en: So they go down the hill.
sentences.zh: 于是他们走下山岗。

sentences.en: They get onto the plain.
sentences.zh: 他们来到了平原上。

sentences.en: The plain is covered with bodies, many of them being mangled by hyenas.
sentences.zh: 平原上到处都是尸体，许多尸体正被鬣狗啃食残缺。

sentences.en: So that's a bit disconcerting.
sentences.zh: 所以这让人感到有些毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: Under their white flag, they get to the British camp.
sentences.zh: 在白旗的掩护下，他们抵达了英军营地。

sentences.en: And when the soldiers see them coming, the soldiers will start cheering.
sentences.zh: 当士兵们看到他们走来时，便开始欢呼雀跃。

sentences.en: And they're taken straight to Napier.
sentences.zh: 他们被直接带去见内皮尔。

sentences.en: And they say to Napier, we've come from the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们对内皮尔说，我们是奉皇帝之命来的。

sentences.en: The emperor wants peace.
sentences.zh: 皇帝想要和平。

sentences.en: And Napier says, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 内皮尔说，太好了。

sentences.en: And Napier dictates a very gracious reply.
sentences.zh: 随后内皮尔口授了一封非常温和体面的回信。

sentences.en: He says, your majesty has fought like a brave man and has been overcome by the superior power of the British army.
sentences.zh: 他说，陛下作战勇敢，却被英军更为强大的力量所击败。

sentences.en: It is my desire that no more blood may be shed.
sentences.zh: 我的愿望是不再流血。

sentences.en: If therefore your majesty will submit to the Queen of England and bring all the Europeans now in your majesty's hands and deliver them safely this day in the British camp,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果陛下愿意向英国女王投降，并将目前在陛下手中的所有欧洲人于今日安全送交英军营地，

sentences.en: I guarantee honorable treatment for yourself and for all the members of your majesty's family.
sentences.zh: 我保证给予您本人以及陛下家属所有成员以荣誉礼遇。

sentences.en: And he says Teodros has 24 hours to decide.
sentences.zh: 并且他说特沃德罗斯只有24小时做出决定。

sentences.en: So the delegation go back to Teodros.
sentences.zh: 于是代表团回到了特沃德罗斯那里。

sentences.en: And he says, I don't really understand what he means.
sentences.zh: 他说，我实在不明白他是什么意思。

sentences.en: What does he mean by honorable treatment?
sentences.zh: 他说的荣誉礼遇是什么意思？

sentences.en: Do they mean to treat me honorably as a prisoner?
sentences.zh: 他们是打算像对待俘虏那样给予我体面的待遇吗？

sentences.en: Or do they intend to assist me in recovering my country from the rebels?
sentences.zh: 还是他们打算协助我从叛军手中收复我的国家？

sentences.en: And I think this is when he's got a real shock at this point.
sentences.zh: 我想这时他真正感到了震惊。

sentences.en: Because I think he always thought that the British would fight him, be impressed by him and his big gun.
sentences.zh: 因为我想他一直以为英国人会与他交战，并对他和他的大炮留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: His guns, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他的大炮，是的。

sentences.en: And then they would help him and they would be great friends.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会帮助他，大家会成为好朋友。

sentences.en: And now he thinks, I don't want to be taken as a prisoner back to London.
sentences.zh: 而现在他想，我可不想作为俘虏被带回伦敦。

sentences.en: That is the last thing that I want.
sentences.zh: 那是我最不愿意看到的事。

sentences.en: So he dictates this very rambling reply.
sentences.zh: 于是他口授了这封语无伦次的回复。

sentences.en: No mention of the hostages.
sentences.zh: 字里行间没有提及人质。

sentences.en: A lot of mention of how terrible the Abyssinian people are.
sentences.zh: 却花了大量篇幅痛陈阿比西尼亚人民有多么糟糕。

sentences.en: A land of heathens, he describes his own country as.
sentences.zh: 他将自己的国家描述为一片异教徒的土地。

sentences.en: He says, you are brilliant people.
sentences.zh: 他说，你们是杰出的人民。

sentences.en: You're a people governed by discipline.
sentences.zh: 你们是一个受纪律约束的民族。

sentences.en: I'm very impressed with you.
sentences.zh: 我对你们印象深刻。

sentences.en: But he doesn't really give Napier a clear answer about the hostages.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有就人质问题给内皮尔一个明确的答复。

sentences.en: He sends this message to Napier's camp.
sentences.zh: 他把这条消息发送到了内皮尔的营地。

sentences.en: Then he goes and sits on a rock alone.
sentences.zh: 然后他独自走到一块岩石上坐下。

sentences.en: His men see him praying.
sentences.zh: 他的手下看到他在祈祷。

sentences.en: They see him bow three times.
sentences.zh: 他们看到他鞠躬三次。

sentences.en: And then to their horror, they see him pull a pistol from his belt and put it in his mouth and go to pull the trigger.
sentences.zh: 接着，在他们惊恐的注视下，他们看到他从腰带里拔出一把手枪放进嘴里，准备扣动扳机。

sentences.en: And his officers rush at him and they yank his arm away.
sentences.zh: 他的军官们冲向他，猛地将他的胳膊拉开。

sentences.en: And he does fire, but the bullet just grazes his ear.
sentences.zh: 他确实开枪了，但子弹只是擦伤了他的耳朵。

sentences.en: I mean, you say to their horror, but I mean, he has led them into a complete disaster.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能会说这让他们感到惊恐，但我的意思是，正是他把他们带向了一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: So they're still loyal to him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们依然忠于他。

sentences.en: But they must be horrified because they stop him shooting himself.
sentences.zh: 但他们一定吓坏了，因为他们阻止了他自杀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because you'd think with all his ranting and his lunatic general behavior.
sentences.zh: 因为你想，他有那么多狂吼和疯狂的举止。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They might think this isn't really the greatest war leader we've ever had.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会觉得，这其实不是我们遇到过的最伟大的战时领袖。

sentences.en: You might think that, but maybe some of them just think it's fun.
sentences.zh: 你可能会这么想，但也许有些人只是觉得好玩。

sentences.en: It's fun.
sentences.zh: 好玩。

sentences.en: You know, you never know where you are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你永远不知道自己身处何地。

sentences.en: No two days are the same.
sentences.zh: 没有哪两天是相同的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Because he's busy chopping off hands and feet, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他正忙着砍手砍脚，不是吗？

sentences.en: And throwing people to hyenas.
sentences.zh: 还把人扔给鬣狗。

sentences.en: Looting manuscripts.
sentences.zh: 掠夺手稿。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's doing that, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，他当然在做这些。

sentences.en: Maybe it's that.
sentences.zh: 也许就是这样吧。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: He now throws himself to the ground.
sentences.zh: 他现在把自己摔在地上。

sentences.en: He's sobbing.
sentences.zh: 他在痛哭。

sentences.en: He's disconsolate.
sentences.zh: 他心灰意冷。

sentences.en: He's just in the floods of tears.
sentences.zh: 他简直泪如泉涌。

sentences.en: And then he dusts himself down.
sentences.zh: 然后他又拍拍尘土站起来。

sentences.en: And for about the 17th time, he says, bring all the Europeans down from the mountaintop.
sentences.zh: 差不多第 17 次，他说，把所有欧洲人从山顶带下来。

sentences.en: It is hard to keep up, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很难跟上，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, you find it hard to keep up.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你觉得很难跟上节奏。

sentences.en: Imagine having to make the notes.
sentences.zh: 想象一下还得做笔记。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对啊。

sentences.en: You just want to keep track of where everybody is.
sentences.zh: 你只想知道每个人都在哪里。

sentences.en: I thought you were going to say, imagine being a hostage.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你要说，想象一下成为人质。

sentences.en: But no, you're the victim here.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，你才是这里的受害者。

sentences.en: No, I'm the real victim in all this.
sentences.zh: 不，我才是这一切中真正的受害者。

sentences.en: Let's be clear.
sentences.zh: 咱们把话说清楚。

sentences.en: So the hostages are dragged back down.
sentences.zh: 于是人质们被拖了回来。

sentences.en: They're completely bewildered.
sentences.zh: 他们彻底迷茫了。

sentences.en: It's very dark.
sentences.zh: 天很黑。

sentences.en: It's a very sort of ominous scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常不祥的场景。

sentences.en: They're convinced that Teodros has gone completely mad and is going to kill them all.
sentences.zh: 他们坚信特沃德罗斯已经彻底疯了，要把他们赶尽杀绝。

sentences.en: They get halfway down and then a guard stops them and he says, Mr. Rassam, please, the rest of you stay here.
sentences.zh: 他们走到半路，一个卫兵拦住他们说，拉斯姆先生，请留步，其余的人留在这里。

sentences.en: Teodros wants to speak to Rassam alone.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯只想单独和拉斯姆谈谈。

sentences.en: Rassam, who's very nervous, finds the emperor standing alone by the edge of the cliff.
sentences.zh: 非常紧张的拉斯姆发现皇帝正独自站在悬崖边。

sentences.en: And Teodros, who's a broken man, says to him, you know, Mr. Rassam, that you and I have always been on good terMs.
sentences.zh: 而心碎的特沃德罗斯对他说，你知道的，拉斯姆先生，你和我一直关系很好。

sentences.en: I've always had a high regard for you.
sentences.zh: 我一直对你高度评价。

sentences.en: It's true I behave badly towards you.
sentences.zh: 我承认我对你态度不好。

sentences.en: But that was because of the behavior of bad men.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为那些坏人的行为。

sentences.en: And Teodros says, tomorrow, when I'm taken prisoner, please stand up for me in the British camp.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯说，明天，当我被俘时，请在英军营地为我仗义执言。

sentences.en: Put a good word in for me.
sentences.zh: 替我美言几句。

sentences.en: I want you to bear this in mind.
sentences.zh: 我想让你记住这一点。

sentences.en: Unless you befriend me, I should either kill myself or become a monk.
sentences.zh: 除非你与我交好，否则我要么自杀，要么当和尚。

sentences.en: Now, goodbye.
sentences.zh: 好了，再见。

sentences.en: It's getting late.
sentences.zh: 天色不早了。

sentences.en: Try to come see me tomorrow if you can.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，明天尽量来看看我。

sentences.en: And they shake hands.
sentences.zh: 然后他们握了握手。

sentences.en: And Rassam sees tears in Teodros's eyes.
sentences.zh: 拉斯姆看到特沃德罗斯眼中含着泪水。

sentences.en: And Rassam goes on down the path.
sentences.zh: 接着拉斯姆顺着小路往下走。

sentences.en: And Rassam is terrified that when he goes on down the path, he will find that all the other hostages have been butchered.
sentences.zh: 拉斯姆吓坏了，生怕顺着小路走下去时，会发现其他所有人质都遭了屠杀。

sentences.en: But no, he meets up with the other hostages.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，他遇到了其他的人质。

sentences.en: And they all now trudge on towards the British camp.
sentences.zh: 于是他们现在一起艰难地朝英军营地走去。

sentences.en: And they pass through the British lines, great cheering.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过英军防线，一片欢呼。

sentences.en: They've all been freed.
sentences.zh: 他们全都获释了。

sentences.en: It's an incredibly emotional scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其感人的场面。

sentences.en: They're shown to Napier's tent.
sentences.zh: 他们被带到纳皮尔的帐篷。

sentences.en: The British agent in Aidan, who was called Colonel Merriweather, has brought loads of champagne along just in case.
sentences.zh: 亚丁的英国特工名叫梅里韦瑟上校，他带了大量的香槟以防万一。

sentences.en: See, I've mentioned the champagne.
sentences.zh: 你看，我提到了香槟。

sentences.en: Who said that's why they brought the champagne, right?
sentences.zh: 谁说这就是他们带香槟的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: So they open the champagne.
sentences.zh: 于是他们打开了香槟。

sentences.en: You know, it's all over.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一切都结束了。

sentences.en: Or is it?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Not quite.
sentences.zh: 不见得。

sentences.en: The next day is Easter Sunday.
sentences.zh: 第二天是复活节星期日。

sentences.en: Teodros is still up on the hill.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯还在山顶上。

sentences.en: Sends Napier another letter.
sentences.zh: 给纳皮尔写了另一封信。

sentences.en: Very erratic.
sentences.zh: 非常反常。

sentences.en: He tells Napier that he's tried to kill himself.
sentences.zh: 他告诉纳皮尔他曾试图自杀。

sentences.en: Satan placed in me the thought that I should die by my own gun.
sentences.zh: 撒旦让我产生了用自己的枪结束生命的念头。

sentences.en: He says, as a peace offering, I'm going to send you a thousand cows and 500 sheep, which he does.
sentences.zh: 他说，作为求和的礼物，我要送你一千头牛和五百只羊，他也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And as the livestock is being led towards the British line, Teodros says to his officers, surely it is peace now.
sentences.zh: 正当牲畜被牵往英军防线时，特沃德罗斯对他的军官们说，现在一定和平了吧。

sentences.en: They've taken my power from me.
sentences.zh: 他们已经剥夺了我的权力。

sentences.en: Surely it is peace.
sentences.zh: 现在肯定和平了。

sentences.en: But now the tragic turning point in the story.
sentences.zh: 但故事悲剧性的转折来了。

sentences.en: Napier refuses to accept the cows and the sheep.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔拒绝接受这些牛羊。

sentences.en: And I think the reason he does this is he knows that under the local custom, if he accepts them, that means it's all over and he's accepted peace.
sentences.zh: 我想他这么做的原因，是他知道按照当地习俗，如果他接受了，就意味着一切都结束了，他也接受了和平。

sentences.en: And when Teodros sees Napier turning them away, he says bitterly to his courtiers, these people having got what they wanted, they now want to kill me.
sentences.zh: 当特沃德罗斯看到纳皮尔把它们赶走时，他痛苦地对朝臣们说，这些人达到了目的，现在又想要我的命。

sentences.en: He flirts with the idea of fleeing.
sentences.zh: 他动过逃跑的念头。

sentences.en: He says, you know, maybe we could run away.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，也许我们可以逃跑。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll get to Lake Tana.
sentences.zh: 也许我们能到达塔纳湖。

sentences.en: But his men say to him, no, we're not going to flee with you.
sentences.zh: 但他的手下对他说，不，我们不会跟你一起逃跑。

sentences.en: You've got to make peace now.
sentences.zh: 你现在必须讲和。

sentences.en: We will stay with your majesty till death.
sentences.zh: 我们将誓死追随陛下。

sentences.en: But you must listen to our advice and come to terms with the Ferenjis, with the foreigners.
sentences.zh: 但你必须听从我们的建议，与费伦吉人、与外国人达成协议。

sentences.en: And Teodros is devastated by this.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯对此感到心碎欲绝。

sentences.en: They won't run away with him.
sentences.zh: 他们不肯跟他一起逃跑。

sentences.en: And that night, he kind of wanders alone on the mountain, staring down at the British campfires.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，他独自一人在山上徘徊，俯视着英国人的营火。

sentences.en: Now, Napier, meanwhile, is down with his senior officers thinking about what to do.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，纳皮尔正和高级军官们在一起商量对策。

sentences.en: Deep down, I don't think they want to know the battle.
sentences.zh: 从心底里讲，我觉得他们并不想打这一仗。

sentences.en: His men are exhausted.
sentences.zh: 他的手下已经精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They've gone a long way.
sentences.zh: 他们走了很长的路。

sentences.en: They're hundreds of miles from home.
sentences.zh: 他们离家数百英里。

sentences.en: They have, of course, now got the hostages.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们现在已经有人质在手了。

sentences.en: They could just turn around and go back at this point.
sentences.zh: 他们完全可以在这个时候掉头回去。

sentences.en: The reason they don't is it's the point that you made earlier on, the similarity with the fall of the Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以不这么做，就是你之前提到的那个原因，和阿兹特克人灭亡的相似之处。

sentences.en: They would have to go through lands controlled by rival warlords.
sentences.zh: 他们必须穿过敌对军阀控制的领地。

sentences.en: And he knows those warlords expect him basically to finish Teodros off.
sentences.zh: 他知道那些军阀基本上指望他除掉特沃德罗斯。

sentences.en: So, basically, the deal is he has to finish Teodros off or else they risk being cut up as they march back to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上交易就是他必须干掉特沃德罗斯，否则他们在返回海岸的途中就会面临被切碎的风险。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think finishing Teodros off might well involve taking him prisoner and bringing him back to London.
sentences.zh: 我想除掉特沃德罗斯很可能包括俘虏他并把他带回伦敦。

sentences.en: And Teodros is probably frightened that he's going to be dragged through the streets in
sentences.zh: 而特沃德罗斯可能害怕自己会在街头被戴上镣铐游街

sentences.en: chains like a captured general in a Roman triumph, which probably would not have been the case.
sentences.zh: 就像罗马凯旋式中被俘的将军那样，不过实际情况可能并非如此。

sentences.en: He would probably have had tea with Queen Victoria Osborne House and then been sort of incarcerated in some country house in Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 他很可能会去奥斯本宫与维多利亚女王喝茶，然后被关押在汉普郡的某个乡村宅邸里。

sentences.en: I mean, worst case scenario, you're being exhibited at a freak show in the East End.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最坏的情况，也就是在东区的怪胎秀上被展览。

sentences.en: No, they wouldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不会那样做。

sentences.en: No, of course they wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他们当然不会。

sentences.en: Of course they wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 他们当然不会。

sentences.en: Well, as we will discover in the bonus episode about what they do with Teodros' son, they send him to public schools.
sentences.zh: 好吧，正如我们将在关于他们如何对待特沃德罗斯的儿子的彩蛋剧集里发现的那样，他们把他送去了公学。

sentences.en: So, anyway, Monday morning, Teodros has been outside all night and he climbs back up to the fortress and his men are huddled around their campfires and they watch him in silence.
sentences.zh: 总之，星期一早上，特沃德罗斯在外面待了一整夜，他又爬回了要塞，他的手下聚在营火旁，静静地看着他。

sentences.en: And Teodros says, come on, death or glory, one last stand, let's attack the British.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯说，来吧，不成功便成仁，最后一战，我们进攻英国人。

sentences.en: Bring your weapons and follow me.
sentences.zh: 带上武器跟我来。

sentences.en: And he leads them out of the citadel down this path.
sentences.zh: 他带着他们走下城堡，顺着这条小路前进。

sentences.en: They get about halfway down the mountain and then a lot of them say, hold on, this is mad.
sentences.zh: 他们走到了山路的一半，然后很多人说，等等，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But I'm not attacking the British again.
sentences.zh: 我可不会再去进攻英国人了。

sentences.en: We would rather seek death in Magdala, they say.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们宁愿在马格达拉求死。

sentences.en: And a very deflated Teodros says, fine, we'll go back.
sentences.zh: 士气低落的特沃德罗斯说，好吧，我们回去。

sentences.en: So they trudge back up again.
sentences.zh: 于是他们又艰难地爬了上去。

sentences.en: God, it's up and down, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 天哪，这上上下下的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's all this story is.
sentences.zh: 我是说，整个故事就是这样。

sentences.en: I know, constant.
sentences.zh: 我懂，没完没了。

sentences.en: He's getting his steps in, that's for sure.
sentences.zh: 他的步数肯定是走够了。

sentences.en: A lot of his men slip away.
sentences.zh: 他的手下逃走了很多。

sentences.en: Yeah, they know this is all over.
sentences.zh: 对，他们知道这一切都结束了。

sentences.en: So by the afternoon of Easter Monday, he's in Magdala with a dwindling band of loyalists and they're sort of stacking boulders against the outer gate.
sentences.zh: 所以在复活节星期一的下午，他在马格达拉与一小群日渐减少的忠诚追随者在一起，他们正把巨石堆在外门后面。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Napier has ordered his guns to start shelling the Abyssinian citadel.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，纳皮尔下令用大炮轰击阿比西尼亚城堡。

sentences.en: And the shells are getting closer and closer.
sentences.zh: 炮弹越来越近了。

sentences.en: By about four o'clock in the afternoon, the first British troops were advancing up the path towards the sort of outer gates.
sentences.zh: 到了下午四点左右，第一批英国军队沿着小路向外门推进。

sentences.en: And the shells are now landing inside the walls between the inner and outer gates.
sentences.zh: 炮弹现在正落在内外城门之间的城墙内。

sentences.en: So Teodros and his remaining loyalists begin to fall back towards the inner gate.
sentences.zh: 于是特沃德罗斯和剩下的死忠开始向内门撤退。

sentences.en: And at this point, the British have brought scaling ladders with them and they start to scale the ladders and to climb the outer ramparts.
sentences.zh: 此时，英国人带来了云梯，他们开始架梯子攀登外城墙。

sentences.en: Some of them get to the outer gate and they start to force open the doors with kind of crowbars and stuff.
sentences.zh: 有些人到达外门，开始用撬棍之类的东西强行撬开大门。

sentences.en: Now, Teodros and his companions are kind of firing at them from the inner gateway, but it's completely pointless.
sentences.zh: 现在，特沃德罗斯和他的同伴们正从内城门向他们开枪，但完全是徒劳。

sentences.en: There are now hundreds of British soldiers streaming up the path and towards the outer gateway.
sentences.zh: 现在有数百名英国士兵顺着小路涌向外门。

sentences.en: And it's at this point that Teodros shouts his last order to his men.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，特沃德罗斯向手下喊出了最后一道命令。

sentences.en: He shouts, flee, I release you from your allegiance, but I shall never fall into the hands of an enemy.
sentences.zh: 他大喊，逃命吧，我解除你们的效忠，但我绝不会落入敌人手中。

sentences.en: And he pulls out a gun and he puts the end in his mouth and he pulls the trigger and bang.
sentences.zh: 他掏出一支枪，把枪口放进嘴里，扣动扳机，砰。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: He falls to the ground.
sentences.zh: 他倒在地上。

sentences.en: And within moments, his men are melted away.
sentences.zh: 转眼间，他的手下作鸟兽散。

sentences.en: The gates have opened and the British troops are pouring in and they see his body lying on the ground in the duSt.
sentences.zh: 大门打开了，英国军队蜂拥而入，他们看到他的尸体躺在尘土中的地上。

sentences.en: And he is, of course, quite dead.
sentences.zh: 当然，他已经死透了。

sentences.en: And by his side lies the gun with which he took his own life.
sentences.zh: 在他的身旁，静静地躺着那把结束了他生命的枪。

sentences.en: And they pick it up and they see it is the silver duelling pistol that he was given as a gift from Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 他们把它捡起来，发现那是维多利亚女王送给他的那支银质决斗手枪。

sentences.en: The one you told us to remember.
sentences.zh: 也就是你让我们记住的那把。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's killed himself with his present from Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 他用维多利亚女王送的礼物自杀了。

sentences.en: You are like Agatha Christie putting the candlestick on the mantelpiece in chapter two.
sentences.zh: 你就像阿加莎·克里斯蒂，在第二章就把烛台放在了壁炉台面上。

sentences.en: That Chekhov's gun.
sentences.zh: 也就是契诃夫之枪。

sentences.en: I introduce the gun in act one and it's going to recur in act five.
sentences.zh: 我在第一幕亮出了这把枪，它将在第五幕再次出现。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that is the end of Teodros, the emperor of Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿比西尼亚皇帝特沃德罗斯的结局。

sentences.en: Dr. Blanc, who had been his hostage, did the postmortem.
sentences.zh: 曾作为他人质的布兰克医生进行了尸检。

sentences.en: And Dr. Blanc said later, death that gave an air of calm grandeur to the features of one whose career had been so remarkable, whose cruelties are almost unparalleled in history.
sentences.zh: 布兰克医生后来写道，这种死亡给一位生平如此卓越、其残酷在历史上几乎绝无仅有的人物，赋予了一种平静而崇高的气度。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's unfair, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这其实挺不公平的。

sentences.en: But who at the last hour fought like a brave man and killed himself rather than surrender.
sentences.zh: 但他却在最后关头像个勇士一样战斗，宁死不降。

sentences.en: And it was actually Mr. Brassam who organised the funeral, which was held in the Coptic church on the Magdala hilltop the next day.
sentences.zh: 事实上是布拉萨姆先生组织了葬礼，第二天在马格达拉山顶的科普特教堂举行。

sentences.en: Teodros, he would have loved that.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯，他肯定会喜欢这样的。

sentences.en: He would have loved that.
sentences.zh: 他一定会喜欢这样的。

sentences.en: That's what he wanted.
sentences.zh: 这正是他想要的。

sentences.en: I mean, he died as he would have wanted in some ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种程度上说，他的死法正是他所渴望的。

sentences.en: And he got the funeral he would have wanted, devised by his beloved.
sentences.zh: 他得到了他梦寐以求的葬礼，由他所爱的人为他设计。

sentences.en: The only thing he'd have liked, I think he'd have liked Queen Victoria to have been there.
sentences.zh: 他唯一会希望的，我想他是希望维多利亚女王当时能在场。

sentences.en: I think no, I think it's all about Rassam.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不，我觉得这全都是因为拉萨姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许吧。

sentences.en: Don't forget, he'd been very rude about Queen Victoria being a woman.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，他之前对维多利亚女王是个女人这件事说过很多很不客气的话。

sentences.en: He had, yes, he had.
sentences.zh: 他确实说过，是的，他确实说过。

sentences.en: So at the end, the other defenders surrendered almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 所以在最后，其他守军几乎立刻就投降了。

sentences.en: And this was the cue for the British to start piling into the manuscripts, the relics and the treasures.
sentences.zh: 这也成了英国人开始疯狂搜掠手稿、遗物和宝藏的信号。

sentences.en: Now, as we said, this is not an entirely straightforward British bad guys plundering stuff story, because
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，这并非一个完全简单的“英国恶棍四处劫掠”的故事，因为

sentences.en: of course, this was stuff that Teodros had basically accumulated in his campaigns.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些东西基本上都是特沃德罗斯在历次战役中积累下来的。

sentences.en: And he had an absolutely mad collection.
sentences.zh: 而且他的藏品简直疯狂。

sentences.en: So he had religious relics and vestments and crowns and goblets.
sentences.zh: 他有宗教圣物、法衣、王冠和高脚杯。

sentences.en: He had a lot of manuscripts.
sentences.zh: 他有大量的手稿。

sentences.en: He had musical instruments.
sentences.zh: 他有乐器。

sentences.en: He had, weirdly, a collection of Staffordshire pottery.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，他还有一堆斯塔福德郡的陶器。

sentences.en: He had umbrellas.
sentences.zh: 他有雨伞。

sentences.en: He had cases of wine.
sentences.zh: 他有一箱箱的葡萄酒。

sentences.en: He had carpets.
sentences.zh: 他有地毯。

sentences.en: He had lion skins.
sentences.zh: 他有狮子皮。

sentences.en: He had toy soldiers and a collection of cameras, all of which ended up in the baggage of all these British soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他有玩具士兵和一个相机收藏，所有这些最终都落入了这群英国士兵的行囊中。

sentences.en: There was a massive looting free-for-all, which only ended when Napier himself arrived, came up the path.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了一场大规模的抢劫狂欢，直到纳皮尔本人抵达并沿着小路走上来才宣告结束。

sentences.en: And he came up with a military band playing God Save the Queen and See the Conquering Hero
sentences.zh: 他伴随着军乐队演奏的《天佑女王》和《征服者凯旋》走了过来

sentences.en: Comes.
sentences.zh: 走了过来。

sentences.en: And Napier said, now, come on, we're British.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔说，好了，振作点，我们是英国人。

sentences.en: We don't want a massive free-for-all.
sentences.zh: 我们不想要这种大规模的哄抢。

sentences.en: We will distribute the booty properly.
sentences.zh: 我们会妥善分配战利品。

sentences.en: And basically, they doled out all the cash to all the troops.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们把所有的现金都分发给了全体部队。

sentences.en: And then a few days later, he held a gigantic auction where all the sort of relics and stuff and the cameras and the Staffordshire pottery was auctioned off to the highest bidders.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他还举行了一场盛大的拍卖会，将各种遗物、相机以及斯塔福德郡陶器拍卖给价高者。

sentences.en: So, we can talk possibly in our bonus about some of the loot.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可能会在我们的特别加更节目中聊聊其中一些战利品。

sentences.en: Well, the notorious one is the Tabots, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，最声名狼藉的就是塔博特圣物匣，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're not books, exactly.
sentences.zh: 它们其实不是书。

sentences.en: They're kind of tablets, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们有点像石板，对吧？

sentences.en: Held by the British Museum, I think, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 据我所知，是由大英博物馆保管的，对吧？

sentences.en: And there's one held by Westminster Abbey, I think.
sentences.zh: 还有一个是由威斯敏斯特教堂保管的，我想是的。

sentences.en: So, we talk about some of the loot in our special bonus episode on this for Rest It's
sentences.zh: 所以，我们会在针对“历史休息室”

sentences.en: History Club members.
sentences.zh: 俱乐部成员的特别加更节目中讨论部分战利品。

sentences.en: We also talk about what happened to some of the hostages, like Hummus, Rassam.
sentences.zh: 我们还会讨论某些人质的结局，比如胡默斯·拉萨姆。

sentences.en: And we talk about two other characters that we haven't really mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论我们之前没有真正提及另外两个人物。

sentences.en: So, one is a guy called Captain Speedy, who was one of Napier's deputies.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是叫斯皮迪上尉的家伙，他是纳皮尔的副手之一。

sentences.en: Literally, Speedy.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，就叫斯皮迪。

sentences.en: That's not his nickname.
sentences.zh: 那不是他的绰号。

sentences.en: That was his name, Captain Speedy.
sentences.zh: 那就是他的名字，斯皮迪上尉。

sentences.en: But Captain Speedy, before this, had been Teodros' military advisor.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，斯皮迪上尉曾是特沃德罗斯的军事顾问。

sentences.en: So, he had an extraordinary career.
sentences.zh: 所以他有着一段非凡的经历。

sentences.en: He knew all about the guns.
sentences.zh: 他对外面的枪炮了如指掌。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: And the other person is Teodros' son, Prince Alamehu.
sentences.zh: 另一个人是特沃德罗斯的儿子，阿拉梅胡王子。

sentences.en: And he was sent back to England.
sentences.zh: 他被送回了英国。

sentences.en: He was introduced to Queen Victoria, and he ended up as a boarder at Rugby, a Flashman's old school.
sentences.zh: 他被引见给了维多利亚女王，最后成了拉格比公学（弗莱什曼的母校）的一名寄宿生。

sentences.en: So, we'll talk about him and his extraordinary trajectory.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们会谈谈他和他那段非凡的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: But back to Napier.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，我们回到纳皮尔。

sentences.en: Now, we talked before about comparisons with other military expeditions, perhaps particularly those launched by our American cousins.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到了与其它军事远征的对比，特别是可能由我们的美国表亲们发起的那些。

sentences.en: And the difference with Napier is Napier has absolutely no interest in installing a client
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔的不同之处在于，他完全没有兴趣扶植一个傀儡

sentences.en: regime, in sorting, you know, making Abyssinia safe for democracy, any of that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 政权，也没有兴趣去收拾残局、让阿比西尼亚对民主安全放心，或者诸如此类的任何事情。

sentences.en: His orders were to get in, get the hostages, and get out again.
sentences.zh: 他的命令是：杀进去，救出人质，然后撤出来。

sentences.en: And that is precisely what he's going to do.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他要做的。

sentences.en: He's not interested in Abyssinia at all.
sentences.zh: 他对阿比西尼亚一点兴趣也没有。

sentences.en: He sends a message to his army the day after the auction.
sentences.zh: 拍卖会结束后的第二天，他向他的军队发了一条消息。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: The Queen and the people of England entrusted to you a very arduous and difficult expedition to release our countrymen from a long and painful captivity
sentences.zh: 女王和英国人民托付给你们一次非常艰巨且困难的远征，旨在解救我们长期遭受痛苦囚禁的同胞

sentences.en: and to vindicate the honour of our country.
sentences.zh: 并捍卫我们国家的荣誉。

sentences.en: We've done it.
sentences.zh: 我们做到了。

sentences.en: We're going home.
sentences.zh: 我们要回家了。

sentences.en: The message that Jimmy Carter never got to deliver.
sentences.zh: 吉米·卡特从未能发表的那番演讲。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, the result of this, actually, is that Abyssinia is left leaderless, and the result is 20 years of chaos.
sentences.zh: 所以，这实际上导致的结果是，阿比西尼亚群龙无首，随之而来的是长达二十年的混乱。

sentences.en: Because, basically, it's like they've gone in and they've kicked over an ant heap, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为这基本上就像他们闯进去捅了一个蚂蚁窝，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Complete chaos.
sentences.zh: 一片混乱。

sentences.en: You sort yourselves out.
sentences.zh: 你们自己看着办吧。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing is, what could they have done?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，问题是，他们还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: They could have chosen a client king.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以选出一个傀儡国王。

sentences.en: It would probably have all ended in disaster, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白讲，那可能最终都会以灾难收场。

sentences.en: I think they absolutely did the right thing in getting out.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们选择撤离绝对是做对了。

sentences.en: There's 20 years of civil war.
sentences.zh: 接下来是二十年的内战。

sentences.en: There's then the war in the Sudan, which spills over.
sentences.zh: 接着是蔓延过来的苏丹战争。

sentences.en: The Mardi, our old friend General Gordon.
sentences.zh: 马赫迪，我们老朋友戈登将军。

sentences.en: And it only ends, really, at the end of the century under a guy called Menelik II.
sentences.zh: 而这一切真正结束，其实是在世纪末一个叫梅内利克二世的人统治时期。

sentences.en: And he really establishes himself as a kind of Abyssinian hero by beating the Italians at the Battle of Adwar in 1896, which is seen as a kind of landmark moment.
sentences.zh: 他在1896年的阿杜瓦战役中击败了意大利人，这被视为一个具有里程碑意义的时刻，从而真正树立了自己作为阿比西尼亚英雄的形象。

sentences.en: Humiliation of a European army by an African one.
sentences.zh: 一个欧洲军队被非洲军队羞辱。

sentences.en: But all that lies in the future.
sentences.zh: 但那都是以后的事了。

sentences.en: So Napier and co.
sentences.zh: 所以纳皮尔一行人

sentences.en: march back to the coast, their bands playing, their flags flying.
sentences.zh: 乐队奏乐，军旗招展，向海岸行军进发。

sentences.en: They get there in June.
sentences.zh: 他们在六月抵达那里。

sentences.en: Everything is loaded back onto the ships, the railway tracks, the telegraph wires, the elephants.
sentences.zh: 一切都被重新装上船，铁路轨道、电报线、大象。

sentences.en: The elephants are all right, are they?
sentences.zh: 大象都安然无恙吧？

sentences.en: The elephants are all right.
sentences.zh: 大象都安然无恙。

sentences.en: The hostages.
sentences.zh: 人质也是。

sentences.en: Eight days later, Napier embarks for Suez.
sentences.zh: 八天后，纳皮尔启程前往苏伊士。

sentences.en: He goes back to England.
sentences.zh: 他回到了英国。

sentences.en: In England, he is a hero.
sentences.zh: 在英国，他是个英雄。

sentences.en: We rejoice that the honour of the British flag and the dignity of the British name have been vindicated.
sentences.zh: 我们欢欣鼓舞，因为英国国旗的荣誉和英国名誉的尊严得到了捍卫。

sentences.en: Asiatics will ponder and talk over the fate of a man who imprisoned British subjects.
sentences.zh: 亚洲人将会深思并议论那个囚禁英国臣民的人的命运。

sentences.en: And they'll think twice about challenging the power that triumphed over the black king.
sentences.zh: 他们将三思而后行，不敢再去挑战那个战胜了黑人国王的力量。

sentences.en: So, quite pungent stuff from British editorials.
sentences.zh: 所以，英国各大社论的措辞可谓相当辛辣。

sentences.en: Napier is given the thanks of Parliament.
sentences.zh: 纳皮尔受到了议会的感谢。

sentences.en: He's given a reception by the Queen.
sentences.zh: 他获得了女王的接见。

sentences.en: He's promoted to field marshal.
sentences.zh: 他被晋升为陆军元帅。

sentences.en: And he's given a hereditary peerage.
sentences.zh: 并被授予世袭贵族爵位。

sentences.en: So, he becomes Baron Napier of Magdala.
sentences.zh: 于是他成为了马格达拉的纳皮尔男爵。

sentences.en: And there's still a Baron Napier of Magdala today.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，依然有马格达拉的纳皮尔男爵这一爵位。

sentences.en: And when he dies in 1890, he's a national hero.
sentences.zh: 当他在1890年去世时，他已是一位民族英雄。

sentences.en: And there's a statue put up in Kensington.
sentences.zh: 肯辛顿竖起了一座他的雕像。

sentences.en: A Queen's Gate.
sentences.zh: 在女王门。

sentences.en: You can still see it today.
sentences.zh: 你今天依然可以看到它。

sentences.en: But talk of statues.
sentences.zh: 但说到雕像。

sentences.en: We should end in Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 我们应该以阿比西尼亚作为结语。

sentences.en: So, Teodros in Abyssinia, or rather Ethiopia as we now call it, is a cult figure today.
sentences.zh: 因此，特沃德罗斯在阿比西尼亚（或者我们现在所说的埃塞俄比亚）如今是一个受人崇拜的人物。

sentences.en: So, in his brilliant book on this, Philip Marsden talks about going to the markets in Addis Ababa and seeing Teodros T-shirts and badges,
sentences.zh: 菲利普·马森在他关于此事的精彩著作中谈到，他去亚的斯亚贝巴的市场时，看到了特沃德罗斯的T恤和徽章，

sentences.en: seeing his image stenciled on the walls of bars.
sentences.zh: 看到他的肖像被喷涂在酒吧的墙壁上。

sentences.en: He's now seen as a patriotic hero who died fighting European imperialism, a kind of symbol of Ethiopian independence.
sentences.zh: 他现在被视为一个抗击欧洲帝国主义而牺牲的爱国英雄，某种程度上成了埃塞俄比亚独立的象征。

sentences.en: And the most obvious reminder of him, you can go to Emperor Teodros Square, which is in the center of Addis Ababa.
sentences.zh: 而关于他最直观的纪念，你可以去位于亚的斯亚贝巴市中心的特沃德罗斯皇帝广场。

sentences.en: And basically, this is a giant roundabout.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一个巨大的环岛。

sentences.en: And unbelievably, this roundabout is situated on, of all things, Churchill Avenue.
sentences.zh: 难以置信的是，这个环岛竟然坐落在丘吉尔大道上。

sentences.en: Who was at the Battle of Omdaman.
sentences.zh: 他曾参加过恩图曼战役。

sentences.en: Who was at the Battle of Omdaman, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，他曾参加过恩图曼战役。

sentences.en: He was no stranger to a sort of Horn of Africa battle.
sentences.zh: 他对非洲之角的某种战斗并不陌生。

sentences.en: Now, there is no statue of Teodros, but you will be pleased to hear that in the middle of this roundabout, there is a replica of his beloved giant gun, Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 现在，这里没有特沃德罗斯的雕像，但你可能会高兴地听说，在这个环岛的正中央，有一尊他心爱的大巨炮“塞瓦斯托波尔”的复制品。

sentences.en: Oh, fabulous.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: So, you could go and see this.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以去参观一下。

sentences.en: If we haven't done a rest of his history trip to Addis Ababa, we'd obviously go to the…
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有组织过一次“历史休息室”的亚的斯亚贝巴之旅，我们显然会去……

sentences.en: But what about the actual gun?
sentences.zh: 但是那门真正的巨炮呢？

sentences.en: Well, this here is the thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关键就在这里。

sentences.en: The real Sebastopol still exists.
sentences.zh: 真正的“塞瓦斯托波尔”依然存在。

sentences.en: 250 miles away from Addis Ababa.
sentences.zh: 距离亚的斯亚贝巴250英里远。

sentences.en: It's half buried on the barren mountaintop of what was once the fortress of Magdala.
sentences.zh: 它半埋在曾经是马格达拉要塞的荒凉山顶上。

sentences.en: There's nothing there now.
sentences.zh: 现在那里什么也没有。

sentences.en: And it was never fired.
sentences.zh: 而且它从未开过火。

sentences.en: No one ever worked out if it worked.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人弄清楚它到底能不能用。

sentences.en: It shows no sign of ever having been fired.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何曾经开过火的迹象。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: So, there it sits, this forgotten relic of this bizarre episode in British and, indeed, African history.
sentences.zh: 所以，它就那样静静地立在那里，作为英国乃至非洲历史上这段离奇插曲的一处被遗忘的遗迹。

sentences.en: And the mad thing about the whole business, as Sir Harry Flashman rightly puts it in his memoir, it could all have been avoided if only Queen Victoria had answered her letters.
sentences.zh: 而整件事最疯狂的地方在于，正如哈里·弗莱什曼爵士在他的回忆录中所言，这一切本都可以避免，只要维多利亚女王回了信。

sentences.en: Well, on the subject of Queen's behaving badly and disastrous consequences ensuing,
sentences.zh: 好啦，说到女王行为不端并导致灾难性后果的话题，

sentences.en: next week we are back with the French Revolution and specifically with the terror.
sentences.zh: 下周我们将回到法国大革命，具体来说是恐怖统治时期。

sentences.en: So, the most dramatic, the most celebrated episode in the whole of the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是整个法国大革命中最具戏剧性、最负盛名的篇章。

sentences.en: This is tumbrils, guillotines, blood flowing in the streets, the deaths of Marie Antoinette,
sentences.zh: 这就是运囚车、断头台、街头血流成河，以及玛丽·安托瓦内特之死，

sentences.en: Danton, Robespierre.
sentences.zh: 丹东、罗伯斯庇尔。

sentences.en: Just incredible drama and a completely blood-soaked climax.
sentences.zh: 简直是不可思议的戏剧性，以及完全被血浸透的高潮。

sentences.en: And that, if you are a member of the Rest is History Club, you will be getting all six episodes this coming Monday.
sentences.zh: 如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员，本周一你就能听到全部六集节目。

sentences.en: And if you're not and you would like to hear the slicing of the guillotine for six solid episodes, you can go to therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是，但又想连续六集听到断头台落下的声音，你可以访问 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: So, huge excitement for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，对此我们感到无比兴奋。

sentences.en: But I think, Dominic, before we go, massive thanks for telling this forgotten but incredibly dramatic story,
sentences.zh: 不过多米尼克，我想在我们离开之前，非常感谢你讲述了这段被遗忘但却极其戏剧性的故事，

sentences.en: simultaneously tragic and darkly comic, as is so often the case with British Imperial history.
sentences.zh: 它既悲惨又带有黑色幽默，正如英国帝国历史中经常出现的那样。

sentences.en: Poor old.
sentences.zh: 可怜的家伙。

sentences.en: Do you feel sorry if it's your dress?
sentences.zh: 如果那是你的裙子，你会觉得遗憾吗？

sentences.en: I really liked him.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢他。

sentences.en: You wouldn't like him if he'd shackled your...
sentences.zh: 要是他给你戴上脚镣，你可就不会喜欢他了……

sentences.en: No, I wouldn't have wanted to be a hostage.
sentences.zh: 不，我可不想当人质。

sentences.en: But I'll tell you what I liked about him.
sentences.zh: 但我得告诉你我喜欢他哪一点。

sentences.en: I liked his style as a letter writer.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他作为书信作家的风格。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I would have loved to get a letter from him.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想收到他的信。

sentences.en: And unlike Queen Victoria, I would have replied and become his pen pal.
sentences.zh: 而且不像维多利亚女王，我会回信并成为他的笔友。

sentences.en: Maybe Rest is History listeners, if those people who feel fondly disposed to Tom, why don't you send in your letters to him in the style of Teodoros II,
sentences.zh: 或许“历史其余部分”的听众们，如果那些对托姆抱有好感的人，你们为什么不模仿狄奥多罗斯二世的风格给他写信呢，

sentences.en: and there'll be a prize for the...
sentences.zh: 而且将会有奖品……

sentences.en: The prize is Tom will take you, just the two of you, on a trip to Sebastopol to inspect the mortar in the middle of nowhere in Ethiopia.
sentences.zh: 奖品是托姆会带你——就你们两个——去塞瓦斯托波尔旅行，去考察埃塞俄比亚荒郊野岭中的那门迫击炮。
